### Be Faithful over Little: A Different Vision for a Life That Counts
Author: Chase Krug
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/faithful-over-little/
Passage: Matthew 25:21
Points:
- Believers often assume that an impactful Christian life requires world-shaping influence or fame.
- The master commends the servants not for being extraordinary, but for being faithful over a little.
- God does not judge by sheer output, as both the two-talent and five-talent servants receive the identical commendation.
- True faithfulness is comprehensive stewardship of the specific opportunities and gifts God provides.
- Most faithful kingdom labor takes place in the quiet, ordinary rhythms of everyday life.

### Able and Available
Author: Renee Swope
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/encouragement/encouragement-04-27-04-1258559.html
Passage: Matthew 25:21
Points:
- With every God-given ability comes an assignment, risk, and personal responsibility.
- Insecurity and comparison can tempt believers to bury their gifts, assuming small contributions do not matter.
- God multiplies ministry impact when we make ourselves available and use what He has placed in our hands.
- Faithfulness in small matters leads to deeper purpose and sharing in the Master's joy.

### Successful or Faithful?
Author: Leslie Snyder
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/homeword/homeword-nov-17-2006-1449052.html
Passage: Matthew 25:21
Points:
- Society and even church culture often evaluate worth by worldly metrics of visible success.
- In the parable of the talents, the master commends the servants for being faithful rather than merely successful.
- The third servant suffered loss because fear led him to bury his talent rather than invest it.
- Believers are called to invest their gifts with excellence and leave the ultimate results to God.

### Investing Your Life
Author: Kelly McFadden
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/homeword/homeword-mar-25-2008-11571570.html
Passage: Matthew 25:19-21
Points:
- Christians should be even more intentional about investing their lives for God than planning their financial futures.
- Everything we have belongs to God, which brings accountability for how our gifts are stewarded.
- Fear and selfish ambition tempt people to hoard or bury their God-given potential.
- God honors and rewards those who proactively dedicate their time and abilities to eternal purposes.
